_doc: Specie, Mints & the Price Level (world/moneySupply.js, systems/mints.js, systems/coinCensus.js). A realm's money is the real coin held in it: each week the census counts every purse in the realm — its towns' purses, its townsfolk's, gangs', guilds', inns', couriers', landholders', rival Houses' and merchant houses', court NPCs', lairs', and the coin carried by caravans and armies on its land — as coin in circulation (world.money.realms[id].coin). The crown's chests, the banks' vaults and the player's purse are held out of circulation (broad money): they move no prices until they are spent. Coin moving between purses inside a realm changes nothing; NPC trade across a border pays town to town; the flows below move real coin out of and into the towns' purses. The realm's price level follows its coin per head (x velocity: hoarding in war and panic) against the world's, smoothed and clamped, and multiplies every price in its markets together with the coin's purity (world/coinage.js). Set enabled false to switch the whole system off (every reader returns neutral). Balance: docs/economy-balance.md 'Specie, Mints & the Price Level'.
_level: Quantity term: the realm's price level target = (coin x velocity / people, against the world's) ^ elasticity, clamped to [min, max]; the level moves `smoothing` of the way there each week. Kept narrow on purpose: a whole-basket gap between two realms is a gap every trader can work.
_velocity: Hoarding: a realm at war hoards `war` of its coin, one with a run on its bank or a fresh crown default `panic` more; velocity moves `adjust` of the way to its target each week (never below `floor`).
_trade: The price-specie flow: NPC traders already pay for the goods that cross a border, town purse to town purse (world/settlementMarket.js). On top, between realms that traded in the week, a realm with less coin per head than its partner is cheaper, sells it more, and wins back hume x the gap in log coin per head x the smaller of the two realms' coin a week, drawn from the partner's towns into its own; so a drained realm recovers. maxShare: most of a realm's coin that leaves it in one week this way.
_gresham: Bad money drives out good: a realm whose coin is debased loses rate x (1 - purity) of its towns' coin a week to its sounder trading partners' towns (merchants hoard and export the old full-weight pieces).
_flight: Coin flight: a realm with a run on one of its banks, or a crown default in the last `defaultDays`, loses `rate` of its towns' coin a week to the soundest realms it trades with.
_wear: Share of the towns' coin lost a week: worn, clipped, buried, carried off to far lands. The mints must keep striking to hold the level.
_drift: The invisible balance: pilgrims, mercenaries' pay, smugglers and travellers carry coin from realms with much of it to realms with little, whether they trade or not. Each week a realm's coin moves by ratio ^ -drift (its coin per head against the world's): what is drawn from the rich realms' towns is paid into the poor realms' towns.
_income: The crown's tax yield follows the coin about (KingdomAI.incomeMultiplier x level ^ elasticity, clamped): a realm drained of coin collects less, one awash in it more. The crowns' daily income is otherwise a ledger of their realms' commerce; see docs/economy-balance.md for why it is only partly backed.
_mint: The mints. Each week every realm's mint buys gold and silver ore from its markets where the stock stands above `keep` x the market's target (at most weeklyFine of fine value, x the mint policy's draw), paying the selling town in new coin, plus what the player sold it (paid in new coin on the spot). fine: coin a unit of bullion holds at full purity (gold ore, 40g base, holds 36; silver ore, 18g, holds 16; a gold bar, 150g, 140). Coin struck = fine / purity (a debased mint strikes more coin from the same bullion); the crown's seigniorage is struck into its treasury, the rest is paid to the sellers. The player is paid fine x (1 - seigniorage) x the realm's price multiplier, never more than `askCap` of the open market's ask for that good here (no buy-here-sell-to-the-mint loop), up to playerWeeklyFine a week per mint. remint: share of the foreign coin that came into circulation during the week (trade receipts, Gresham, flight) brought to the mint to be restruck as the realm's own, for the same seigniorage drawn from the towns' purses into the treasury: most of a mint's profit in a realm without mines.
_recoinage: A recoinage edict calls in the coin in the towns' purses and strikes it anew at full purity. Holders get back purity + crownShare x (1 - purity) of each piece (the towns' purses shrink: prices fall); the crown pays crownShare x (1 - purity) x that coin from its treasury (its silver goes into the new coin), and the realm's stability moves `stability`. A crown out of trouble (debt ratio under maxDebtRatio, treasury above treasuryCover x the cost) proclaims one by itself; the player as ruler may at any time. Not again within cooldown days. (Debasement, systems/finance.js: the holders get back as many pieces as they brought; the crown keeps the extra pieces in its treasury, and they swell the coin in circulation as it spends them.)
_exchange: Money changers: carrying gold into a realm whose coin is of another purity costs perPurity x the purity gap of the gold carried (at most max), when the purse holds at least minGold and was not assayed in the last cooldownDays (a traveller criss-crossing a border pays once, not at every crossing). Recorded as 'exchange' in the ledger. The rate shown between two coins is their silver content (purity) ratio.
_concession: Leasing a mint: the player pays fee = feeShare x the mint's average weekly seigniorage (last seignHistory weeks) x share x the term's weeks up front into the treasury, and takes `share` of the seigniorage each week for termDays. Not to be had while at war with the realm, from a mint that struck nothing, or while another lease runs.
_counterfeit: Passing false coin (Thieves' Guild members of rank minRank and above, in a settlement of a realm): stake [minStake, maxStake] of good coin in silvered copper, passed for gain x the stake on success. Caught with chance base + heatPer x heat - rankCut x rank, x (looser + (1 - looser) x the coin's purity): a debased coin is easier to fake. Caught: the stake is lost, a fine of fineShare x the stake, heat +caughtHeat, and arrest with arrestChance. Passed: heat +passHeat, and the player's purse is up by the gain — new coin made from copper, which swells the realm's coin as it is spent. Once every cooldown days.
_news: The heralds and the townsfolk: a coin shortage (level at or below shortAt and falling) or a flood of coin (level at or above floodAt and rising) is news once per realm every gapWeeks; recoinages always. Counsel: warn the ruler when their realm's level is outside [shortAt, floodAt] or its coin is debased; tell the player when bullion in their packs would fetch at least bullionGain over the market at a mint within mintRadius hexes.
